postings.title: Accounting intern - Paris
postings.description:
Qui sommes-nous?

Artefact est une nouvelle génération de cabinet de conseil spécialisée en Data dont plus de 2500 collaborateurs répartis sur 27 pays ont pour mission d’accompagner la transformation chez nos clients.

Nous offrons une large gamme de solutions data-driven, que nous adaptions aux besoins spécifiques de nos clients, que ce soit des projets IA pour l'automatisation des process internes à chaque étape de leur chaîne de valeur, la création d'expériences consommateurs innovantes et personnalisées, le conseil en stratégie data et marketing digital jusqu'à la gestion du mix-média et plus encore !

La performance de nos services data repose sur une réelle expertise technologique en Intelligence Artificielle et des compétences métiers acquises auprès de plus de 1000 clients dans le monde, tels que Orange, Carrefour, Engie, Emirates, Deutsche Telekom, Monoprix… 

La force d'Artefact repose sur un mix unique d'atouts: une connaissance des technologies de pointe en data, des méthodes agiles permettant de délivrer très rapidement les projets et des équipes composées des meilleurs experts dans leurs domaines (business consultants, data analysts, data scientists, ingénieurs data…).

Dans ce contexte, nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) stagiaire Assistant Comptable pour rejoindre notre équipe finance en janvier 2027.

Missions : 

Sous la responsabilité du Responsable Comptable France, vous assurez la gestion de l’état administratif financier de l’entreprise.

De ce fait, vous contribuerez avec l’équipe finance France à :

Factures fournisseurs :

- Collecter les factures et informations manquantes auprès des fournisseurs et équipes métiers

- Contrôler les factures dès leur réception,

- Valider ces dernières auprès des différentes équipes,

- Saisir les factures fournisseurs dans le logiciel Sage,

- Mettre à jour et contrôler les codes analytiques des écritures comptables

- Analyser les comptes fournisseurs (lettrages, justifications des soldes)

Note de Frais :

- Contrôler et valider les notes de frais, 

- Les intégrer dans Sage

Divers :

- Participer à l’amélioration des outils de gestion (Yooz, Sage 1000, Reporting BI…)

- Réaliser diverses tâches administratives,

- Aider à la préparation de la clôture semestrielle

La variété des diverses tâches qui vous seront attribuées vous permettra d'enrichir vos connaissances et de contribuer à l’amélioration de notre service

Profil : 

- Vous préparez un diplôme dans le domaine de la gestion, comptabilité, contrôle, audit, finance et vous justifiez idéalement d’une première expérience professionnelle (en stage par exemple) sur un poste similaire.

- Vous maîtrisez les techniques comptables et les logiciels informatiques du métier (Idéalement Sage, le pack office). 

- Organisé, enthousiaste, vous êtes reconnu(e) pour votre énergie, votre autonomie et votre sens de responsabilité.

- Vous avez l’esprit d’équipe et vous êtes à l’aise en communication, tant orale qu’écrite.

Salaire : 1200€ brut / mois 

Processus de Recrutement

- Call RH

- Entretien avec le Responsable Comptabilité 

- Entretien avec le Directeur Comptable 

Chez Artefact, nous recrutons nos collaborateurs uniquement en fonction de nos besoins et des qualités propres de chaque candidat. Nous assurons le développement de leurs compétences professionnelles et de leurs responsabilités sans discrimination d’aucune sorte, notamment de croyances, de genre, d’âge, de situation d'handicap, d’origine ethnique, d’orientation sexuelle, d’appartenance à une organisation politique, religieuse, syndicale ou à une minorité.

Come join us!

postings.title: AI & Agentic Engineer, Senior
postings.description:
Join the most advanced community of AI makers.

Mission

Make AI work, beyond the prototype. You build the AI applications, platforms and data that the world's leading companies use every day, and you keep them running in production. Our clients work in retail, luxury, healthcare, financial services and manufacturing.

For example, a customer advisor gets a drafted answer with its sources. An analyst asks a question in plain words and gets the same figure as the finance team. A client team launches a new agent on a platform that already handles access rights and monitoring.

Activities & Responsibilities

Who you work with

You work in project teams with AI Product Managers, who manage the product with the client, and AI Architects, who design the end-to-end solution. Every day, you work with engineers from the other archetypes and with the client's business and IT teams.

You review code with your peers, pair on hard problems and help newer colleagues learn the job. Each archetype has its own community, with representatives who share practices across projects.

One title, four archetypes

Everyone in the chapter has the same title and the same foundation skills. Each person also has one main archetype, defined by the layer of the system they build, with skills specific to that archetype.

- Product Engineer: Applications and agents used in business processes, for the business and its end users. Typical projects: Business applications (front end, back end, APIs); assistants embedded in a process; process automation.

- Platform Engineer: Infrastructure and AI platforms that run products and agents at scale, for engineers and agents. Typical projects: Cloud and infrastructure as code; CI/CD, MLOps and LLMOps; agent runtime and observability; security foundations.

- Context & Analytics Engineer: Data and knowledge that products and agents rely on, for the business and its agents. Typical projects: Ingestion pipelines and data models; data quality; semantic layer and metrics; knowledge pipelines for RAG.

- ML & AI Applied Scientist: The LLM part of applications and agents: context, retrieval, tool use, evaluation, model choice, for the business and its end users. Typical projects: LLM assistants and agents; document processing; evaluation pipelines; fine-tuning a smaller model.

Your main archetype follows your projects of the last 12 months, so it can change when your work changes. You don't need to choose an archetype before applying: the hiring process assesses which one fits your experience.

What you do

Whatever your archetype, you practise the foundation skills:

- Software craft: write code that is tested, reviewed and documented.

- Production ownership: own what you ship after launch, including monitoring, incidents and fixes.

- AI evaluation: define and run evaluations for AI features, and say when AI is not the right tool.

- AI system security basics: manage access rights and secrets, and guard against prompt injection.

- AI-assisted development: write the specification, delegate to coding agents, review the result and keep token costs under control.

- Product and business sense: build for users, ship a first version, measure adoption, improve it.

- Client relationship: explain your choices to clients and manage your part of the project.

Required Skills

Must-haves:

- You build software in Python, TypeScript, SQL or another language, and you can explain how it works as a whole, including the parts a coding agent wrote.

- You have built something people use in one of these areas: applications, infrastructure, data or LLM applications. Work, internships and study projects all count.

- You treat monitoring, incidents, costs and security as part of the job.

- You explain technical choices clearly to people who are not engineers.

Bonus, not required:

- Experience evaluating AI or machine learning systems.

- Client-facing experience.

You don't need to tick every box to apply. If you match most must-haves and want to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

What we expect at your level

- Senior: owns a workstream of their archetype end to end, splits and estimates the work, reviews code and works autonomously with the client.

What to expect / Recruitment process

The process has five interviews. You don't need to choose an archetype before applying: after the HR interview, interviews 2 to 4 are run by engineers from the archetype that fits your experience, with a case from that archetype. Each archetype's interview focus is described in its section above.

- HR interview (45 min): your background and current situation, your fit (autonomy, client posture, teamwork) and your interest in building AI systems.

- Technical interview (60 min) with an engineer from your archetype: the fundamentals of your archetype (live coding for Product and Context & Analytics, cloud and DevOps for Platform, maths, ML and LLM evaluation for ML & AI Applied Scientists), then a deep dive on something you built.

- System design (60 min) with two engineers from different archetypes: design the AI system for a client use case, go deep on your part (application, platform, data and context, or model) and defend your choices.

- Hands-on build (60 min) with an engineer from your archetype: build a working piece of the previous case with the tools of your choice, AI coding assistants included, then demo it and walk through it.

- Fit interview (30 min) with a Director: meet the team and learn how we work.

About Artefact

Artefact is the trusted AI deployment team to the world's leading companies: 3,000 AI makers in more than 30 countries and more than 1,000 clients. In the US, you join the Engineering & Deployment department, in the AI Applied Engineer chapter.

Diversity & Inclusion

Artefact is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on skills and potential, and we welcome applicants of every background, identity and experience. If you need an adjustment at any step of the hiring process, tell your recruiter.

Why Join Artefact

At Artefact, data and AI are not abstract strategy topics. They are tools for creating business value, improving organizations, and helping people make better decisions.

You will join a global community of data and AI experts who combine consulting, engineering, data science, marketing, and technology expertise. You will work on complex, high-impact problems with leading organizations and help shape how enterprises adopt AI responsibly and effectively.

We value action, collaboration, learning, client trust, and shared knowledge. We believe that technology only matters when it is used, adopted, and translated into impact.

Our values aren't decorations on a wall — they're how we actually work:

- There is always a way — We're builders and problem-solvers. An idea only counts if it gets executed.

- Client trust is won in the field — We show up, sleeves rolled up, working side by side with our clients.

- If it's not used, it's useless — We build for adoption and impact, not for slide decks.

- If it's not shared, we're not done — Knowledge shared compounds. We invest in each other's growth.

- We learn every day — In a field that moves this fast, standing still means falling behind. We embrace the challenge.

How We Support Our People

In addition to our values-driven culture, we offer a range of benefits and programs designed to support our employees' growth and well-being, including:

- Learning and Development: Work alongside a multidisciplinary team of AI, data, and consulting experts who are committed to continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and professional growth.

- Hybrid Flexibility: Our hybrid work model gives you the flexibility to balance collaboration, client needs, and personal commitments.

- Comprehensive Benefits: We offer a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company matching, and paid parental leave.

- Time to Recharge: We believe sustainable performance matters. That's why we offer unlimited paid time off, giving you the flexibility to take the time you need.

- Growth Opportunities: As a rapidly growing organization, you'll have the opportunity to expand your skills, take on new challenges, and help shape the future of the company.

postings.title: AI applied Engineer
postings.location: Capital Tower, Boulevard Mly Youssef, Casablanca, Maroc
postings.description:
Mission

Join the most advanced community of AI makers.

New models arrive every month, open or closed: you choose which ones are good enough for production, and you prove it. You build applications and agents on top of large language models (LLMs) and make the model part work. Our clients use these systems to answer customers, process documents and search their own knowledge.

You decide what context the model gets, how it retrieves knowledge and which tools it can call. You measure how good its answers are, and choose the model that fits the cost and quality target.

This role is for you if you want to know whether an AI system gives correct answers, not only whether it runs.

Artefact is the trusted AI deployment team to the world's leading companies. In France, you join its Engineering department, about 300 people, in the AI Applied Engineer chapter and the AI Engineer archetype.

Activities & Responsibilities

Who you work with

Product Engineers build the application around the model; you own how the model behaves inside it. Context Engineers prepare the knowledge your agents retrieve, and Platform Engineers own the shared harness, runtime and model-serving infrastructure; you own the agent logic and behaviour that runs on it.

With the AI Product Manager and the client's domain experts, you define what a good answer is and review results together. You review code with your peers and help newer colleagues.

What you do

- Build Machine learning applications, such as scoring or time series forecasting, with all the necessary steps: data wrangling, training loops, cross validation, evaluation, and deployment. 

- Build LLM applications and agents: context design, tool calling, multi-step workflows.

- Design how agents use knowledge: retrieval queries, re-ranking, citations.

- Build evaluation sets and pipelines: reference answers, automated scoring, review by domain experts.

- Track answer quality in production and fix what degrades.

- Choose models by quality, cost and latency. Fine-tune or distil a smaller model when prompting is not enough.

- Add guardrails against wrong answers, data leaks and prompt injection.

- Process documents with LLMs: extraction, classification, summaries.

Required Skills

Must-haves:

- You have built an application or agent that calls an LLM, and you can explain where it worked and where it failed.

- You write tested, maintainable code.

- You already use coding agents in your daily work and check what they produce.

- You measure AI output quality with test sets and metrics, and you know how to limit made-up answers, prompt injection and data leaks.

- You know what it takes to put an LLM application in production and keep it there: deployment, monitoring, cost and latency.

- You start from the business problem, not the model, and you can explain to non-engineers when AI is not the right tool.

Bonus, not required:

- Fine-tuning or distillation of language models.

- A background in machine learning or statistics, for example from data science.

- Agent frameworks or protocols such as MCP.

- Multimodal inputs: documents, images, speech.

- LLM observability tools: tracing, cost tracking.

You don't need to tick every box to apply. If you match most must-haves and want to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

postings.title: AI Applied Engineer
postings.description:
Who We Are

Artefact is an applied AI company. We build systems that run in production, in our clients' own cloud, and keep running after we leave. We are present in 27 countries across all continents with a team of 2,500 employees and offer the most comprehensive set of AI & data solutions per industry, built on deep data science and cutting-edge AI technologies, delivering AI projects at scale in all industry sectors. From strategy to operations, we partner with 1000+ clients, including some of the world’s top 300 brands.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Deployed AI Engineer specialized in Gemini Enterprise and the Google AI stack: an engineer who works embedded with our clients and takes AI products from idea to production.

You will design and build the interfaces, services, and agentic systems at the heart of our client work, such as conversational applications over enterprise data, multi-step agents that automate business workflows, and the retrieval and data pipelines that support them. You will own your components end to end: the front end, the service behind it, the data and retrieval pipelines feeding it, the deployment, and the evaluations proving it works.

This role combines deep, certified expertise in Google's enterprise AI stack (Gemini models, Vertex AI, and the Gemini Enterprise agent platform) with the ability to deliver end to end. Beyond your platform specialization, you will be expected to work confidently across the full delivery lifecycle — full-stack development, data engineering, cloud infrastructure, evaluation, and client communication.

You will work closely with our clients, with direct exposure from the start, and you will support the professional development of the engineers around you.

What You'll Do

Build Full-Stack AI Applications, End to End

You will build AI products across the entire stack, from interface to infrastructure.

- Develop user-facing interfaces and the backend services and APIs behind them in Python.

- Implement agentic behavior: orchestration, tool and function calling, memory, and guardrails.

- Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector and hybrid search.

- Connect AI systems to enterprise data and applications via APIs, semantic layers, and protocols such as MCP.

Go Deep on Gemini Enterprise and the Google AI Stack

You will be the team's reference for Google's enterprise AI platform.

- Design and build agents with Gemini models, Vertex AI, the Agent Development Kit (ADK), and Agent Engine.

- Implement and configure Gemini Enterprise for clients: Agent Designer for natural-language and trigger-based agents, the Inbox for managing long-running agents at scale, and agent sandboxes for autonomous problem-solving.

- Connect Gemini Enterprise to the client's application landscape through first-party and partner connectors, with proper permissions, governance, and auditability.

- Build grounded, retrieval-backed applications with Vertex AI Search and RAG Engine, grounding with Google Search, and BigQuery as the data backbone.

- Implement agent interoperability through the A2A protocol and MCP.

- Track Google's releases closely and translate new capabilities into client value quickly.

Make AI Systems Production-Grade

Our standard is production quality: systems that are reliable, monitored, and maintainable.

- Write evaluation suites and regression tests for LLM-powered features, and monitor cost, latency, and quality in production.

- Apply solid engineering practice: version control, code review, automated testing, CI/CD, and observability.

- Deploy on cloud infrastructure (GCP, Azure, or AWS) using containers, serverless, and infrastructure-as-code.

- Build and maintain the data pipelines that feed AI systems, across warehouses, lakehouses, and vector stores.

Work AI-Natively and Client-Facing

Our engineers work AI-natively and represent Artefact directly with clients.

- Use agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor) daily, with good judgment about verification and review.

- Communicate progress, trade-offs, and blockers clearly to clients and project leads.

- Support pre-sales when needed: scope solutions, build demos, and estimate effort with our partnership and consulting teams.

- Mentor junior engineers and contribute to internal accelerators, reusable components, and engineering standards.

What We're Looking For

- 1–3 years of experience in software engineering or data engineering, with extensive hands-on use of AI tools and LLM-based development over the past year (professional projects, internal initiatives, or substantial personal builds).

- Strong hands-on experience with the Google AI stack: Gemini models, Vertex AI, and ideally Gemini Enterprise or ADK — ideally with experience taking at least one solution to production on GCP.

- Strong programming skills in Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, and experience building and consuming APIs.

- Experience with front-end development (React or similar) and at least one backend framework.

- Hands-on experience with RAG, embeddings, and vector search, and with at least one agentic framework (Google ADK, LangGraph/LangChain).

- Strong working experience with GCP; Azure or AWS is a plus.

- Fluency with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, or Cursor.

- Experience building and maintaining data pipelines.

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Why you should join us:

- Learning and Development: Join a team of passionate Consultants always ready to help each other, providing opportunities to learn and collaborate with some of the best in the field.

- Culture of Celebration: We pride ourselves on creating a collaborative and fun work environment with regular team events and activities.

- Competitive Rewards: Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including a competitive salary, phone & travel reimbursements, remote work allowance, and a Onefit membership discount.

- Work-Life Balance: We offer flexibility with a hybrid working environment that lets you balance personal and professional commitments.

- Fuel Your Day: Enjoy a healthy and delicious daily lunch from our extensive organic buffet.

- Weekly Unwind: Take advantage of our weekly massage sessions to de-stress and relax.

- Centrally Located: Our office is conveniently situated near the station for easy commuting.

- Career Growth Opportunities: We’re committed to your professional development, offering continuous learning and internal promotion opportunities.

Join Us Now and Be Part of the Future:

Artefact is experiencing exciting growth, and this is the perfect time to join our dynamic team and contribute to our success story.
Come join us!

postings.title: AI Applied Engineer
postings.description:
Mission

De nouveaux modèles, ouverts ou fermés, sortent chaque mois : encore faut-il choisir ceux qui sont assez bons pour la production, et le démontrer. Applications et agents s’appuient sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM), et la partie modèle de ces systèmes est entre vos mains. Nos clients s’en servent pour répondre à leurs propres clients, traiter des documents et interroger leurs connaissances.

Ce que le modèle voit, la manière dont il retrouve les connaissances, les outils qu’il peut appeler : ces choix vous appartiennent, de même que la mesure de la qualité des réponses. Le modèle retenu doit tenir l’objectif de coût et de qualité.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez savoir si un système d’IA donne des réponses justes, et pas seulement s’il tourne.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype AI Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités

Les Product Engineers construisent l’application autour du modèle ; le comportement du modèle à l’intérieur vous revient. Les Context & Analytics Engineers préparent les connaissances que vos agents retrouvent, et les Platform Engineers exploitent le serving, le harness et l’observabilité sur lesquels vous vous appuyez.

Avec l’AI Product Manager et les experts métier du client, une bonne réponse se définit, puis les résultats s’examinent ensemble. La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

- Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.

- Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.

- Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.

- Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.

- Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.

- Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.

- Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

- Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.

- Votre code est testé et maintenable.

- Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

- La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.

- Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.

- Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

- Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.

- Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.

- Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.

- Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.

- Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype AI Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (responsabilité en production, bases de la sécurité de l’IA).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

- Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

- Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 53 000€ à 70 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + variable selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

postings.title: AI Applied Engineer
postings.description:
Join the most advanced community of AI makers.

This role is in the ML & AI Applied Scientist archetype of the AI Applied Engineer chapter. Everyone in the chapter has the same title and the same foundation skills. Each person also has one main archetype, defined by the layer of the system they build, with skills specific to that archetype.

Mission

New models arrive every month, open or closed: you choose which ones are good enough for production, and you prove it. You build applications and agents on top of large language models (LLMs) and make the model part work. Our clients use these systems to answer customers, process documents and search their own knowledge.

You decide what context the model gets, how it retrieves knowledge and which tools it can call. You measure how good its answers are, and choose the model that fits the cost and quality target.

When an off-the-shelf model is not enough, you also build and adapt the models themselves: forecasting and optimisation engines, fine-tuned or distilled models, and the evaluation frameworks that prove a model is good enough.

This role is for you if you want to know whether an AI system gives correct answers, not only whether it runs.

Who you work with

Product Engineers build the application around the model; you own how the model behaves inside it. Context & Analytics Engineers prepare the knowledge your agents retrieve, and Platform Engineers own the shared harness, runtime and model-serving infrastructure; you own the agent logic and behaviour that runs on it.

With the AI Product Manager and the client's domain experts, you define what a good answer is and review results together. You review code with your peers and help newer colleagues.

What you do

- Build machine learning applications, such as scoring or time series forecasting, with all the necessary steps: data wrangling, training loops, cross validation, evaluation, and deployment.

- Build LLM applications and agents: context design, tool calling, multi-step workflows.

- Design how agents use knowledge: retrieval queries, re-ranking, citations.

- Build evaluation sets and pipelines: reference answers, automated scoring, review by domain experts.

- Track answer quality in production and fix what degrades.

- Choose models by quality, cost and latency. Fine-tune or distil a smaller model when prompting is not enough.

- Add guardrails against wrong answers, data leaks and prompt injection.

- Process documents with LLMs: extraction, classification, summaries.

- Frame the modelling problem with the AI Product Manager and the business: the objective, the constraints and the metric that matters.

- Build forecasting and optimisation engines, and take them to production with Platform Engineers.

- Design evaluation frameworks and benchmarks for models and agents, including reinforcement learning where it helps.

- Run model research and benchmarking, and turn the results into reusable assets for the chapter.

- Explain model behaviour, uncertainty and limits to business stakeholders.

Required Skills

Must-haves:

- You have built an application or agent that calls an LLM, and you can explain where it worked and where it failed.

- You write tested, maintainable code.

- You already use coding agents in your daily work and check what they produce.

- You measure AI output quality with test sets and metrics, and you know how to limit made-up answers, prompt injection and data leaks.

- You know what it takes to put an LLM application in production and keep it there: deployment, monitoring, cost and latency.

- You start from the business problem, not the model, and you can explain to non-engineers when AI is not the right tool.

- You have a solid foundation in machine learning and statistics: you can explain why a model works and when it will fail.

Bonus, not required:

- Fine-tuning or distillation of language models.

- Agent frameworks or protocols such as MCP.

- Multimodal inputs: documents, images, speech.

- LLM observability tools: tracing, cost tracking.

- Forecasting, optimisation or reinforcement learning in production.

- Publications, patents or open-source models.

You don't need to tick every box to apply. If you match most must-haves and want to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

Tech grid skills that matter most: ML, Optimization & Foundation Models; Applied Math, Statistics & AI Evaluation; AI & Agentic Solutions.

Certifications (a plus): Databricks Machine Learning Professional, Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer.

Interview focus: Technical interview: maths, ML and LLM evaluation fundamentals. System design: go deep on the model or agent behaviour and how you evaluate it. Hands-on build: an LLM or ML component for the case and the evaluation that proves it works.

Foundation skills, whatever your archetype

- Software craft: write code that is tested, reviewed and documented.

- Production ownership: own what you ship after launch, including monitoring, incidents and fixes.

- AI evaluation: define and run evaluations for AI features, and say when AI is not the right tool.

- AI system security basics: manage access rights and secrets, and guard against prompt injection.

- AI-assisted development: write the specification, delegate to coding agents, review the result and keep token costs under control.

- Product and business sense: build for users, ship a first version, measure adoption, improve it.

- Client relationship: explain your choices to clients and manage your part of the project.

What we expect at your level

- Senior: owns a workstream of their archetype end to end, splits and estimates the work, reviews code and works autonomously with the client.

What to expect / Recruitment process

The process has five interviews. You don't need to choose an archetype before applying: after the HR interview, interviews 2 to 4 are run by engineers from the archetype that fits your experience, with a case from that archetype. Each archetype's interview focus is described in its section above.

- HR interview (45 min): your background and current situation, your fit (autonomy, client posture, teamwork) and your interest in building AI systems.

- Technical interview (60 min) with an engineer from your archetype: the fundamentals of your archetype (live coding for Product and Context & Analytics, cloud and DevOps for Platform, maths, ML and LLM evaluation for ML & AI Applied Scientists), then a deep dive on something you built.

- System design (60 min) with two engineers from different archetypes: design the AI system for a client use case, go deep on your part (application, platform, data and context, or model) and defend your choices.

- Hands-on build (60 min) with an engineer from your archetype: build a working piece of the previous case with the tools of your choice, AI coding assistants included, then demo it and walk through it.

- Fit interview (30 min) with a Director: meet the team and learn how we work.

About Artefact

Artefact is the trusted AI deployment team to the world's leading companies: 3,000 AI makers in more than 30 countries and more than 1,000 clients. In the US, you join the Engineering & Deployment department, in the AI Applied Engineer chapter.

Diversity & Inclusion

Artefact is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on skills and potential, and we welcome applicants of every background, identity and experience. If you need an adjustment at any step of the hiring process, tell your recruiter.

Why you should join us

We are united by our values and strengthened by our hybrid expertise.

- There is always a way: We're from the breed of does, of diggers, of makers. Because ideas are valuable only if executed.

- Client trust is won on the field: Addressing client needs flows better hands on at their side.

- If not used, it is useless: Our love for technology translates into a steep desire for adoption, true brilliance is about impact.

- If not shared, our work is not done: Sharing knowledge is the best way to button up a mission, benefitting clients and colleagues.

- We learn everyday: Tech is a land where everything move at the speed of light, you better be ready to challenge yourself.

How We Support Our People

In addition to our values-driven culture, we offer a range of benefits and programs designed to support our employees' growth and well-being, including:

- Learning and Development: Work alongside a multidisciplinary team of AI, data, and consulting experts who are committed to continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and professional growth.

- Hybrid Flexibility: Our hybrid work model gives you the flexibility to balance collaboration, client needs, and personal commitments.

- Comprehensive Benefits: We offer a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan with company matching, and paid parental leave.

- Time to Recharge: We believe sustainable performance matters. That's why we offer unlimited paid time off, giving you the flexibility to take the time you need.

- Growth Opportunities: As a rapidly growing organization, you'll have the opportunity to expand your skills, take on new challenges, and help shape the future of the company.

The estimated base compensation for this role is $125,000 - $135,000 (NYC location). Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, this role is eligible for competitive benefits.

postings.title: AI Applied Engineer
postings.description:
Mission

De nouveaux modèles, ouverts ou fermés, sortent chaque mois : encore faut-il choisir ceux qui sont assez bons pour la production, et le démontrer. Applications et agents s’appuient sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM), et la partie modèle de ces systèmes est entre vos mains. Nos clients s’en servent pour répondre à leurs propres clients, traiter des documents et interroger leurs connaissances.

Ce que le modèle voit, la manière dont il retrouve les connaissances, les outils qu’il peut appeler : ces choix vous appartiennent, de même que la mesure de la qualité des réponses. Le modèle retenu doit tenir l’objectif de coût et de qualité.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez savoir si un système d’IA donne des réponses justes, et pas seulement s’il tourne.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype AI Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités

Les Product Engineers construisent l’application autour du modèle ; le comportement du modèle à l’intérieur vous revient. Les Context & Analytics Engineers préparent les connaissances que vos agents retrouvent, et les Platform Engineers exploitent le serving, le harness et l’observabilité sur lesquels vous vous appuyez.

Avec l’AI Product Manager et les experts métier du client, une bonne réponse se définit, puis les résultats s’examinent ensemble. La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

- Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.

- Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.

- Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.

- Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.

- Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.

- Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.

- Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

- Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.

- Votre code est testé et maintenable.

- Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

- La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.

- Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.

- Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

- Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.

- Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.

- Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.

- Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.

- Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype AI Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (responsabilité en production, bases de la sécurité de l’IA).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

- Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

- Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

- Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

- Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

- Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

- Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 66 000€ à 85 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + variable selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

postings.title: AI Applied Engineer - AI Engineer
postings.description:
Mission

Join the most advanced community of AI makers.

New models arrive every month, open or closed: you choose which ones are good enough for production, and you prove it. You build applications and agents on top of large language models (LLMs) and make the model part work. Our clients use these systems to answer customers, process documents and search their own knowledge.

You decide what context the model gets, how it retrieves knowledge and which tools it can call. You measure how good its answers are, and choose the model that fits the cost and quality target.

This role is for you if you want to know whether an AI system gives correct answers, not only whether it runs.

Artefact is the trusted AI deployment team to the world's leading companies. In France, you join its Engineering department, about 300 people, in the AI Applied Engineer chapter and the AI Engineer archetype.

Activities & Responsibilities

Who you work with

Product Engineers build the application around the model; you own how the model behaves inside it. Context Engineers prepare the knowledge your agents retrieve, and Platform Engineers own the shared harness, runtime and model-serving infrastructure; you own the agent logic and behaviour that runs on it.

With the AI Product Manager and the client's domain experts, you define what a good answer is and review results together. You review code with your peers and help newer colleagues.

What you do

- Build Machine learning applications, such as scoring or time series forecasting, with all the necessary steps: data wrangling, training loops, cross validation, evaluation, and deployment. 

- Build LLM applications and agents: context design, tool calling, multi-step workflows.

- Design how agents use knowledge: retrieval queries, re-ranking, citations.

- Build evaluation sets and pipelines: reference answers, automated scoring, review by domain experts.

- Track answer quality in production and fix what degrades.

- Choose models by quality, cost and latency. Fine-tune or distil a smaller model when prompting is not enough.

- Add guardrails against wrong answers, data leaks and prompt injection.

- Process documents with LLMs: extraction, classification, summaries.

Required Skills

Must-haves:

- You have built an application or agent that calls an LLM, and you can explain where it worked and where it failed.

- You write tested, maintainable code.

- You already use coding agents in your daily work and check what they produce.

- You measure AI output quality with test sets and metrics, and you know how to limit made-up answers, prompt injection and data leaks.

- You know what it takes to put an LLM application in production and keep it there: deployment, monitoring, cost and latency.

- You start from the business problem, not the model, and you can explain to non-engineers when AI is not the right tool.

Bonus, not required:

- Fine-tuning or distillation of language models.

- A background in machine learning or statistics, for example from data science.

- Agent frameworks or protocols such as MCP.

- Multimodal inputs: documents, images, speech.

- LLM observability tools: tracing, cost tracking.

You don't need to tick every box to apply. If you match most must-haves and want to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

postings.title: AI Architect
postings.description:
Présentation du poste :

Concevoir une architecture d’IA, c’est engager une entreprise pour plusieurs années : l’emplacement des données, la gestion des accès, la manière dont un agent passe en production sous le regard des équipes de sécurité. Ces choix structurants, vous les construisez avec nos clients.

Tout le reste, ce sont les ambitions fonctionnelles et techniques du client, son cadre réglementaire, son budget, les compétences qu'il peut réellement mobiliser en interne, la gouvernance qu'il veut installer, et un écosystème d'éditeurs qui gravite autour de lui. Votre rôle est de trouver le point d'équilibre entre ces forces, de le faire accepter, puis de le réajuster dès que l'une d'elles bouge.

Votre point de départ n’est pas la technologie, mais l’ambition métier. Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.

À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.

Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.

Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, vous rejoignez le département Engineering (environ 300 personnes, sous la responsabilité du CTO), au sein du chapter AI Architect.

Activités et responsabilités :

Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.

Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.

Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.

Vos responsabilités :

- Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT comprennent, et défendre vos choix devant eux.

- Concevoir des plateformes data et agentiques, on premise, dans le cloud ou en hybride.

- Découper les périmètres techniques en fonction de la façon dont les équipes du client sont organisées.

- Arbitrer entre les options en pesant leur valeur métier, leur coût total, leur conformité, leur dépendance à un éditeur et la capacité du client à les faire vivre.

- Aider le client à évaluer et à mettre en concurrence des éditeurs, sans parti pris.

- Préparer les propositions commerciales : cadrer la solution, la chiffrer et construire la roadmap de delivery.

- Tenir la ligne pendant le delivery : relire les designs, trancher les arbitrages et réajuster la cible quand le contexte du client change.

- Faire vivre les patterns de référence et les bonnes pratiques du chapter, et suivre de près les évolutions de l’IA, du cloud et de la data.

Profil recherché :

Nous recherchons une personne qui pense comme un consultant et raisonne comme un ingénieur. Les architectes qui réussissent chez nous sont, entre autres, des profils techniques passés par le conseil, des pre-sales engineers, des FDEs, ou des personnes avec une expérience en tant que CTO.

Les indispensables :

- Vous avez conçu une architecture data ou IA qui a été mise en production, et vous savez expliquer pourquoi vous avez écarté les autres options, techniques ou non.

- Vous avez déjà recommandé une option techniquement moins séduisante parce qu'elle correspondait mieux au budget, aux compétences, à la gouvernance ou à la réglementation du client.

- Vous maîtrisez au moins un grand cloud (Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS) ainsi que les fondamentaux de la sécurité et du réseau : IAM, gestion des secrets, architecture réseau.

- Vous avez rédigé des dossiers d’architecture (HLD et LLD) qui ont servi de base à une équipe de delivery.

- Vous avez codé pendant une partie significative de votre parcours. Aujourd'hui, vous savez lire du code, challenger un design et dire ce qu'exige un système en production : CI/CD, monitoring, gestion des incidents.

- Vous avez déjà cadré et chiffré une solution, par exemple pour une proposition commerciale ou un plan projet.

- Vous avez défendu une architecture à la fois devant une direction métier ou un comité de direction, et devant les équipes sécurité et exploitation, en reliant la valeur business, les choix techniques et le plan de delivery.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

- Architecture de plateformes agentiques : RAG, orchestration multi-agents, choix des technologies couche par couche.

- Gouvernance des données à l’échelle d’une grande entreprise : data mesh, gestion des accès.

- Plateformes on premise, hybrides ou souveraines, basées sur des technologies open source ou sur Kubernetes.

- Standards de run : SLA, PRA et PCA.

- Une expérience de CTO, de tech lead ou dans un rôle au contact des clients.

- Une certification d’architecture cloud.

- Une pratique régulière des coding agents.

Ce poste n'est probablement pas pour vous si votre expertise porte sur une seule plateforme ou un seul éditeur et que vous souhaitez continuer à l'approfondir. Ni si construire et écrire du code est ce qui vous anime le plus : le rôle d'AI Applied Engineer vous correspondra mieux.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Process de recrutement :

- HR Interview (30-45 min) : Échange sur votre parcours, vos compétences managériales et l'adéquation culturelle avec un Talent Acquisition Specialist.

- Architecture Case (60 min) : Session d'architecture avec un AI Architect basé en France sur un cas basé sur une vraie mission.

- US / Manager Interview (60 min) : Échange avec un Director / Partner pour évaluer le fit managérial, opérationnel et la posture client.

Rémunération : Package : 75 000 € à 85 000 € brut annuel (fixe) + 8 000 € de variable, selon expérience et séniorité.

Présentation de l’entreprise

Artefact est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en data et en intelligence artificielle, qui accompagne les entreprises pour transformer ces technologies en impact business concret et mesurable.

A la croisée du conseil, de la data et de la technologie, nos 2 500 collaborateurs dans 27 pays mettent leurs expertises en commun pour concevoir, développer et déployer des solutions qui répondent aux enjeux de transformation de nos clients.

Envie d'en savoir plus? Découvrez Artefact, nos expertises et notre culture : https://www.artefact.com

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l'adéquation avec le rôle.

postings.title: AI Architect
postings.location: Capital Tower, Boulevard Mly Youssef, Casablanca, Maroc
postings.description:
Mission

Join the most advanced community of AI makers.

You design how the world’s leading companies run AI at scale, and you make sure it can be built. You start from what the client’s business needs and design the data and agentic platforms that deliver it within their IT landscape, on premise, in the cloud or both. You then stay with the delivery teams until the solution runs in production.

For example, a client’s teams launch each new agent on a shared platform that already handles access rights, monitoring and costs, instead of rebuilding them for every use case. [Example to add: one architecture the chapter delivered, the client’s industry and what changed, without client names.]

This role is for you if you want to see the whole system and own the decisions that are hard to reverse.

Artefact is the trusted AI deployment team to the world’s leading companies: 3,000 AI makers in more than 30 countries and more than 1,000 clients. In France, you join its Engineering department, about 300 people led by the CTO, in the AI Architect chapter.

Activities & Responsibilities

Who you work with

You work in project teams with AI Applied Engineers, who build and run what you design, and with AI Product Managers, who manage the product with the client. You agree on the target with the client’s business leaders. You also work with their IT, security, network and operations teams, so that the architecture fits their landscape and they support it.

You review designs with delivery teams, coach architects and engineers, and share what works with the rest of the chapter. You also work with technology partners and other Artefact teams.

What you do

- Turn the client’s business objectives, constraints and deadlines into an architecture that business and IT stakeholders can follow, then present and defend your choices.

- Design data platforms and agentic platforms, on premise, in the cloud or hybrid.

- Fit the solution to the client’s organisation by defining technical perimeters that match how their teams work.

- Shape proposals: scope the solution, estimate effort and cost, and structure the delivery roadmap.

- Guide delivery: review designs, arbitrate trade-offs during implementation, and make sure the teams can build what you designed.

- Define the chapter’s reference patterns and best practices, and keep up with what changes in AI, cloud and data.

Required Skills

Must-haves:

- You have designed a data or AI architecture that went into production, and you can explain the options you rejected and why.

- You know at least one major cloud (Google Cloud, Azure or AWS) in depth, and you apply security and network fundamentals: IAM, secrets management, network architecture.

- You have written high-level and low-level design documents that a delivery team built from.

- You code in at least one language, such as Python, and you use coding agents in your daily work. You know what it takes to keep a system in production: CI/CD, monitoring, incident management.

- You have scoped a solution and estimated its effort and cost, for example for a proposal or a project plan.

- You link business value, technical choices and a delivery plan, and you explain them clearly to business and IT stakeholders.

Bonus, not required:

- Agentic platform architecture: RAG, multi-agent orchestration, choosing technologies layer by layer.

- Data governance at enterprise scale: data mesh, access management.

- On-premise, hybrid or sovereign platforms built on open-source technologies or Kubernetes.

- Run standards: SLAs, disaster recovery and business continuity plans.

- Experience as a CTO, as a tech lead or in a client-facing role.

- A cloud architecture certification.

You don’t need to tick every box to apply. If you match most must-haves and want to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

postings.title: AI Architect
postings.description:
Who/What is Artefact?
Artefact is a next-generation strategy and data consulting firm dedicated to transforming organizations through data and AI. We combine the rigor of top-tier strategy consulting with deep expertise in data, digital, and analytics to help clients achieve tangible
business impact.
With 1,800+ consultants, data scientists, and engineers across 23 countries, we work with global leaders such as Samsung, L’Oréal, Orange, and Sanofi. Our Zurich office is at the heart of Artefact’s growth, advising clients on their most pressing strategic challenges — from AI strategy and governance to digital transformation roadmaps and new business model design.

The role:

We are looking for a Manager who leads strategy and architecture projects focused on GenAI solutions. You will own the design of architectures and solutions end to end, balancing business value, technology choices and economics across every dimension of the decision.

You will lead development teams, present solutions to C-level stakeholders and run technical and strategic workshops independently.

Key responsibilities:

Project and programme leadership

- 

Lead strategy and architecture projects on GenAI, from scoping and business case through to solution design and rollout oversight.

- 

Own project plans, budgets, risks and quality, ensuring delivery against client objectives.

- 

Shape proposals, estimates and demos, and identify follow-on opportunities with clients.

GenAI architecture and solution design

- 

Design GenAI architectures and solutions: RAG, agentic systems, multi-agent orchestration, MCP and A2A integration, copilots and assistants.

- 

Select and combine cloud-native AI services (e.g. Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, Vertex AI, Bedrock, Databricks) with third-party and custom components.

- 

Apply GenAI to support functions such as HR, Procurement, Legal, Finance and IT, redesigning processes and operating models around the new solutions.

Cross-dimension optimization and trade-offs

- 

Orchestrate decisions across make, buy and customization options, weighing capex against opex and total cost of ownership.

- 

Assess the impact of tool and architecture choices on vendor lock-in, performance, latency, scalability, security and compliance.

- 

Translate these trade-offs into clear recommendations that business and IT leaders can act on.

Team and stakeholder leadership

- 

Guide development teams technically: set the architecture, review solutions and unblock delivery.

- 

Present solutions and recommendations to C-level audiences.

- 

Run technical and strategic workshops independently, from discovery to design and prioritization.

- 

Coach and develop consultants and architects in the team.

Requirements:

- 

At least 8 years of professional experience in IT.

- 

At least 3 years on AI/GenAI architecture and solution design projects.

- 

Prior hands-on background as an engineer or developer.

- 

Proven experience applying GenAI to support functions (HR, Procurement, Legal, Finance or IT).

- 

Consulting experience, ideally in strategy consulting, combined with experience at a system integrator or delivery firm.

- 

Track record of managing projects and leading teams, including development teams.

- 

Experience presenting to C-level stakeholders and running workshops independently.

- 

Excellent written and spoken English.

Technical and functional skills:

- 

GenAI architectures: RAG, agentic and multi-agent patterns, LLMOps, model evaluation, guardrails and responsible AI.

- 

Agent protocols and copilots: MCP, A2A, Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio, custom assistants and their integration with enterprise systems.

- 

Cloud AI platforms: Azure AI Foundry, Vertex AI, Bedrock, Databricks and the native data and AI services of Azure, AWS and GCP.

- 

Architecture trade-offs: make vs buy vs customize, capex vs opex, TCO, lock-in, performance, latency, scalability, security and compliance.

- 

Support functions: processes and operating models in HR, Procurement, Legal, Finance and IT, and how GenAI changes them.

- 

Delivery leadership: agile methods, technical team guidance, solution review, programme governance.

- 

Business: business cases, value tracking, and the ability to translate technical choices into economic impact for executives.

Nice to have:

- 

German not strictly required.

Cloud or AI certifications (e.g. Azure AI Engineer, Azure Solutions Architect, AWS Machine Learning).

postings.title: AI Builder
postings.description:
Who We Are

Artefact is a leading global consulting company dedicated to accelerating the adoption of data and AI to positively impact people and organizations. We build systems that run in production, in our clients' own cloud, and keep running after we leave. 2,000+ people across 27 countries and 1,000 clients, including some of the largest consumer brands in the world. Not a strategy house that discovered AI eighteen months ago, and not a prototype shop that hands you something you will rebuild from scratch.

Three ingredients make that possible, and very few firms have all three: the data, real and messy and at enterprise scale; an applied AI team that can put a model into a governed production environment; and the transformation muscle to make people actually use it. 

Agentic AI lands on marketing and commerce before it lands anywhere else. Agents browse, compare and buy; clicks stop meaning what they meant; the shelf turns into an API. Every CMO and CCO we talk to is asking the same two questions – am I still visible, and can I still prove what worked – and almost nobody can answer them.

What you will be doing

You will own the hardest question in marketing: what actually caused the sales. Marketing Mix Modelling, incrementality testing, geo-lift, attribution – for brands where a three percent reallocation of budget is worth more than most consulting engagements.

And the question is getting stranger. Alongside the media work, you will sit close to three things we build: synthetic brand personas, designed end to end from character bible and voice through to the generative video and avatar pipeline that produces them, running in the client's own cloud with human authorship and copyright chain documented; AI creative studios that generate brand-consistent product imagery and video at retail scale; and trend intelligence engines that detect a movement, predict where it goes, and explain why it matters commercially – early enough to change what a business actually makes.

None of this has a settled measurement stack. Proving it works is the same discipline as proving a television budget worked, applied to something nobody has measured before. That is also you. You will do it as a hands-on scientist and as a trusted advisor to the CMO – both, not either.

What that looks like day to day:

- Direct access to the frontier labs. We work with Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and Mistral as partners, not vendors on a procurement list – early access, joint bets, and the freedom to build with what shipped this quarter rather than what was safe two years ago.

- You own the outcome, not the deliverable. We are in the client's environment from day zero and still there after launch. No prototype handoffs. When something breaks in production, you are close enough to see it and fix it.

- Problems worth your brain. Bayesian MMM at group and geo level. Calibrating models against live experiments. Privacy-constrained measurement where the easy signal has disappeared. Working through identification assumptions with people who care as much as you do about getting them right.

- A direct line to the CMO. Not a workstream lead reporting up through three layers. You present the method, you defend it, you own the recommendation – and you're in the room during qualification, before anything is signed.

- Room to shape the offer. Measurement is not a finished product. You will help decide what we productise next, what we stop doing, and how we take it to market.

- People who make you better. You will work alongside scientists, engineers, creatives and strategists who will pick your models apart and then help you fix it. Nobody here ships alone, and nobody is left to fail quietly.

What We Are Looking For

Seven things. The first four are non-negotiable – if you don't tick every box but the problem interests you, write to us anyway.

- Deep marketing measurement expertise. Around eight years of building, not just presenting, MMM, incrementality and attribution work, or the depth to match. You have shipped models that changed how a real budget was spent, and you can talk about the ones that failed.

- Genuine marketing fluency. You know how retail media behaves differently from paid social, why brand-building resists short-term measurement, and what a media planner is actually going to do with your output on Monday morning. Measurement without marketing intuition produces confident nonsense.

- Serious data science. Causal inference and Bayesian methods as a working craft, not vocabulary. Comfortable across the wider toolkit – forecasting, optimisation, applied GenAI – and still writing code. You would rather debug it than delegate it.

- CMO-grade communication. You can hold a technical audience for an hour on the identification strategy and a CMO for ninety seconds on what to do about it, and be trusted by both. This includes saying "the result is inconclusive" when it is.

- Production instincts. MLOps and cloud industrialisation. A model living in a notebook is a hobby, not a deliverable.

- Presence before the contract. You are in the room during qualification and solution design, not handed a signed scope. Buyers judge us on the calibre of the person in front of them – often that is the whole evaluation.

- AI-native ways of working. You use AI on your own work daily. If you would rather keep the ways of working you already know, ours will frustrate you.

You'll thrive here if you'd rather be wrong in production than right in a slide, you use AI to do your own work rather than just talk about it, you care more about the client's problem than your method, you want feedback more than agreement, and you'd take the harder question.

Would be nice, not required: exposure to the Nordics, published work or conference speaking on measurement, experience blending data science with GenAI content production, a background in optimisation or supply-chain problems alongside marketing, or a master's/PhD in a quantitative field (or a body of work that makes the question irrelevant).

Why you should join us:

- Learning and Development: Join a team of passionate Data Consultants always ready to help each other, providing opportunities to learn and collaborate with some of the best in the field.

- Culture of Celebration: We pride ourselves on creating a collaborative and fun work environment with regular team events and activities.

- Competitive Rewards: Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including a competitive salary, phone & travel reimbursements, remote work allowance, and a Onefit membership discount.

- Work-Life Balance: We offer flexibility with a hybrid working environment that lets you balance personal and professional commitments.

- Fuel Your Day: Enjoy a healthy and delicious daily lunch from our extensive organic buffet.

- Weekly Unwind: Take advantage of our weekly massage sessions to de-stress and relax.

- Centrally Located: Our office is conveniently situated near the station for easy commuting.

- Career Growth Opportunities: We’re committed to your professional development, offering continuous learning and internal promotion opportunities.

Join Us Now and Be Part of the Future:

Artefact is experiencing exciting growth, and this is the perfect time to join our dynamic team and contribute to our success story.
Come join us!

Notre culture inclusive et tournée vers l'avenir encourage la créativité, la collaboration et l'épanouissement professionnel.

- Réaliser des revues d'opportunités régulières avec la direction.

- Polyglotte : La maîtrise de l'anglais est requise ; la maîtrise du néerlandais ou du français est un atout majeur pour le marché belge.

Qualités personnelles

- Leadership transversal et capacité d’influence sans lien hiérarchique direct.

- Sens du service aux métiers et compréhension des enjeux opérationnels terrain.

- Curiosité technologique, ouverture à l’innovation et volonté de créer de la valeur concrète.

postings.description:
Lead the missions where large groups place their AI bets, and turn them into measurable results.

Mission

AI, and agentic AI in particular, is among the priorities of executive committees. At Artefact, we are makers. “We Make AI Work”: our job is not to talk about AI, it is to make it work, at scale, at the heart of large companies. And it all starts with you.

As an AI Strategist Manager, you build with our clients’ leaders a credible AI strategy, a fit-for-purpose operating model and a transformation programme that generates measurable value. You are the engine of our AI Strategy missions: you lead them autonomously, own their quality, deadlines and profitability, grow the consultants staffed on them and develop your accounts alongside Directors and Partners.

You start where every AI transformation begins: with the client’s ambition, industry and business processes, not with the technology. And you stay a maker: you don’t stop at the slide. You build analyses, business cases and working demos yourself (vibe coding, low-code, no-code) that clients can actually touch, and you develop deep expertise in an industry or business function.

You work hand in hand with our Engineering teams (building and delivering agentic AI solutions) and our AI Adoption teams (fostering their adoption): you define the target processes and the roadmap, Engineering builds and delivers them, and AI Adoption guides people through the change, from day one.

Activities & Responsibilities

I. AI strategy & transformation design

You define the AI vision and the prioritised use case roadmap, challenge whether AI is the right answer and own the trade-offs. When relevant, you lead end-to-end process reshapes, thinking lean before deploying AI and mobilising the Engineering and AI Adoption teams to deliver them. You design the target operating model and secure its conditions for success.

II. Analysis, business cases & prototyping

You design and steer the analytical work of the mission, business cases included, to secure data-driven, fact-based decisions, and you review the team’s work. You quickly prototype use cases to illustrate value through demos and help clients project the end solution.

III. Delivery, deliverables & collaboration

You lead missions day to day and give client sponsors visibility: you split each mission into streams, anticipate risks and push back on the client when relevant. You produce C-level deliverables and executive summaries autonomously, structure the storyline and make sure Artefact quality standards are met. You orchestrate the Engineering teams for technical feasibility and the AI Adoption teams to anchor adoption in the field.

IV. Client relationship & business development

You act as the trusted counterpart of business directors and project leads (Comex-1): you map the balance of power among stakeholders, lead restitutions to win buy-in and maximise client NPS, and handle tensions and escalations while preserving trust. You detect new needs on the ground, build the account development plan with the Director or Partner and proactively trigger proposals to grow existing accounts, contributing to commercial proposals and pitches.

V. Team & knowledge

You manage and grow junior and senior consultants, act as counsellor for several colleagues and take part in recruiting future talent. You also contribute to the internal knowledge base through articles and lessons learned, and deliver internal trainings.
